summary: Teams of 2-4 students create a 3-5 minute video revealing what is hidden behind digital spaces like social media, gaming, AI, influencers, or online learning. The project must include a script, storyboard, interactive elements, and follow BPA guidelines. Teams present their video and answer judges' questions, with scoring based on creativity, technical quality, and presentation skills.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Teams will have no more than four (4) hours to plan the storyline and complete all production phases including filming and exporting the video (Nationals only)
submission_requirements: Submit all required items in one combined PDF
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Follow BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
Secure a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including oneself, whose image or work is used in the project
Cite all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
(National only) Film equipment (computer, software, camera, etc.)
competencies: Apply audience analysis and user-centered design principles & elements to create and refine storylines using digital storyboarding and scripting, ensuring clear messaging and engagement for a defined target audience across web, social, and mobile platforms

Utilize video production software, hardware, and workflows to plan, capture, and edit high-quality video content, incorporating nonlinear editing techniques, transitions, audio mixing, sound design, titles, and visual effects to enhance storytelling and production value
Employ camera and lighting techniques—including shot composition, movement, framing, and modern lighting setups—to capture visually engaging footage that meets professional standards

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Team submitted the correct information, in the correct format, as one (1) PDF file.
1. Clickable URL to Video
2. Script
3. Storyboard
4. Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual )
5. BPA Release Form (s)
6. AI Usage and Documentation Form
Included more than one (1) camera angle
At least 75% of the video footage by team members
Final video promotion made effective use of time and was within video time limit of three to five (3:00-5:00) minutes.

rubric.description: The video is very creative and original. Ideas are fresh, bold, and clearly show your unique voice and thinking.
The topic is clearly explained and well thought out. Details are strong, Interesting, and show deep understanding.
The message is clear, strong, and keeps the target audience interested.
Music and tone clearly match the mood and message.
Video is very steady, clear, and well-framed. Shots enhance the viewer’s focus.
Lighting is clear, well-balanced, and enhances the look and feel of the video.
Colors are well -chosen and clearly support the topic, mood, and message.
Audio is clear, smooth, and well-balanced. Fades, effects, and foley are used creatively and effectively.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

rubric.criterion: Included more than one camera angle
Final export met timed event deadline

rubric.description: Entire video shot on-site with creative approach.
Engaging, well-developed, and compelling storyline.
Production elevates the message and viewer experience.
The message is clear, strong, and keeps the target audience interested.
Smooth, sharp shots that enhance professionalism.
Lighting enhances mood and scene clarity.
Vibrant and cohesive color grading throughout.
Excellent use of fades, ambient sound, and normalization.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
